_Apricot Filling - Cooking Method:_

The longer it cooks, the more the flavors come together. You can get away with cooking it for 15-20 minutes, but if you have the time, let it simmer 1-2 hours. Make sure to keep the heat at a low simmer. You want to see some bubbles but nothing too crazy; you don't want it to burn. Stir every so often. If too much liquid evaporates and the sauce gets too thick, stir in some water or chicken broth to reach the desired consistency.
Spread batter into a 12" x 9" baking pan coated with cooking spray.  Sprinkle evenly with remaining chocolate chunks, cranberries and nuts.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven 28-32 minutes or until a deep golden brown.  Cut into squares.
Adjust 2 racks to divide the oven into thirds.  Line cookie sheets with parchment paper.*
Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt and set aside.
Place the butter in a small pan over low heat to melt.  Then set it aside to cool but do not let it harden—it must stay liquid.

Beware! The tomato passata can splatter, so a taller pot is preferred. Cover the pot with a splatter guard if you have one. If you don't have a splatter guard and the tomato is jumping out of the pot, you can partially cover the pot, just don't cover it all the way to make sure the steam can escape.

Shortly before you're ready to eat, boil water and cook pasta according to package directions. This sauce is traditionally served with malloreddus, but tastes great on any pasta shape. It is also fantastic on spaghetti squash.
Melt the remaining 1 cup of chocolate chips in the top of a small double boiler over warm water on low heat, stirring until completely smooth.  Turn off the stove.

Cover one or two cookie sheets with wax paper.  Dip the bottom of each cookie in the melted chocolate and smooth with a small spatula, making a thick layer.  After you spread the chocolate on a cookie, place it chocolate side down on the lined cookie sheet.  Refrigerate until the chocolate is firm and the cookies can be lifted easily.  Place them in an airtight box.  (Use wax paper between the layers.)  Store in the refrigerator.  Let them sit out a bit before serving.

_To make base:_ Line a 15" x 10" x1" baking pan with foil, leaving a 2" overhang on the 2 short sides.  Butter all 4 sides (but not the bottom).  Blend flour, brown sugar, and salt in food processor, then add butter and pulse until mixture begins to form small, pea-size lumps.  (Or you can do this by hand with a pastry blender.)  Sprinkle into baking pan, then press down firmly all over with a metal spatula (and/or fingers) to form an even layer.  Bake at 350° until golden and firm to the touch, 15-20 minutes.  Cool in pan on a rack.

_To make topping:_ Melt butter in a 3-qt. heavy saucepan over moderate heat and stir in sugar, corn syrup, and salt.  Boil over moderately high heat, stirring occasionally, until caramel registers 245° on candy thermometer, about 8 minutes.  Carefully stir in cranberries, then boil until caramel returns to 245°.  Remove from heat and stir in vanilla, then stir in pecans until well coated.  Working quickly, spread caramel topping over base, using a fork to distribute nuts and berries evenly.  Cool completely.

_To cut and decorate:_ Lift bars in foil from pan and transfer to cutting board.  Cut into bars.  Place chocolate in heavy-duty plastic sealable bag.  Microwave on high for 45 seconds; knead bag to mix.  Microwave at additional 10-second intervals, kneading until smooth.  Cut a small hole in bag’s corner; squeeze and drizzle over base.*
They freeze well.
In a small bowl, stir together yogurt, coconut, peanuts, chutney, curry, and ginger.  Gently stir in shrimp.   Fill phyllo cups with mixture and place on cookie sheet.  Bake at 375° for ~8 minutes.
Put beef in a large (about 6-quart) pot with ½ pot of water.  Bring to a boil.  Remove scum.

In the morning, grease a 9" x 13" baking dish and spread the bread cubes evenly in the dish.  Sprinkle the almonds over the bread mixture.  Melt the butter in a Pyrex measuring cup in the microwave (about 40 seconds) and combine with the remaining brown sugar.  Drizzle over the top.

Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20-25 minutes.  Sprinkle with raspberries.  Bake 5-10 minutes longer or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.  (May be ready sooner, so check before adding raspberries and time it accordingly.)
Halves well into 1½-quart baking dish or 9" Cape May fluted dish.
_Apricot variation (for half-recipe):_

Cut 1¼ cups of dried California apricots in half.  Place in pot with ¾ cup of orange juice and ¾ cup of triple sec.  Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer until just about all of the liquid is absorbed, 30 – 60 minutes?  Place in strainer over bowl.  Save liquid in bowl to use as topping.  (It will have consistency of lemon curd.)  Separate apricots (they will be mushy) and place on a board to dry out a bit.  Place in a covered container, separating layers with wax paper.  In the morning, gently stir half of the apricots into bread cubes in batches.  After drizzling with brown sugar/butter, top with remaining apricots.  Eliminate raspberries.  Serve with leftover boiling liquid.
In a bowl, combine all ingredients except fish and mix well.  (Can be made and refrigerated up to 8 hours before using.)

Place the fish flat side down in a baking dish just large enough to hold the fish.  Rub the marinade into both sides of the fish, including the cavities.  If using fish fillet with skin, place in dish skin-side down.  Pour marinade over.  Roast at 450° for about 15 minutes or until fish just begins to flake when prodded with a fork.  Transfer the fish to dinner plates.  Spoon the accumulated sauce over the fish and serve at once.
Melt semi-sweet chocolate, unsweetened chocolate and butter in a double boiler over simmering water; set aside.
Beat eggs, white and brown sugars, and vanilla until light and fluffy.  (Used electric mixer.)
In a separate bowl, toss together the flour, baking soda, salt, pecans, chocolate chips, and dried fruit; set aside.
Pour melted chocolate mixture into egg/sugar mixture and combine thoroughly.  Stir in dry ingredients.  Set aside for a few minutes until mixture cools and batter is firm enough to scoop.
Grease a 9" round pan.  If not using one with rotating sweep, line bottom with parchment and grease again.

Line baking sheets with parchment.  Drop batter by teaspoonfuls onto sheets.  Bake at 375° for about 6 minutes—just until the tops begin to crack and the insides are still fudgy.  Cool on the baking sheets for 10 minutes, then transfer to rack.  When completely cool, store in airtight container.  Recipe says makes 3 dozen cookies.  Made 88 cookies
In a large saucepan (used 3-quart) combine mushrooms, broth, green onion, barley, basil, an pepper.  Bring to boil.*
Reduce heat; cover and simmer ~10 minutes or until barley is tender.
Stir in corn and milk.
Add ingredients (I) and cook a while (maybe 45 minutes or so).
Add ingredients (II).  Cook longer (maybe an hour).
Add celery greens.
Simmer a _total_ of 3 hours over low heat.  Add water if necessary.  Season to taste.
Cook and stir until heated through.
Cut squash in half lengthwise.  Remove seeds and stringy portion.
Place squash, cut side down, in 1 inch of boiling salted water in a kettle.  Bring back to boiling; cover.
Cook 15 minutes or until tender.  Drain on paper towels.
Scoop pulp into bowl with a spoon.  Discard shells.
Mash squash.  Heat oven to 375°.
Melt butter in saucepan over medium heat.  Add flour; cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add milk syrup, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.  Stir until thick and smooth.
Remove from heat.  Add egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in squash and sugar.
Beat egg whites stiff but not dry.  Stir about ½ cup egg whites into squash to lighten it.  Fold squash into remaining egg whites gently.
Turn into buttered 1½-quart soufflé dish.  Smooth with spatula.
Bake 35 - 40 minutes.
Stir together flour, baking powder, and salt in small bowl.

Put butter in large bowl and mix on medium speed for 15 seconds.  Add sugars and beat until butter and sugars are creamed thoroughly, about one minute.  Decrease speed to low and mix in eggs, dissolved espresso, and vanilla, mixing just until eggs are incorporated.  Mixture will look curdled.  Stop mixer and scrape sides of bowl once during mixing.  Slowly add flour mixture and mix just until flour is incorporated and mixture is smooth.  Stir in chips.

Spread evenly into greased 13" x 9" x 2" pan.  Bake at 325° until a toothpick inserted in center no longer has liquid clinging to it, but brownies still feel soft, 28 – 30 minutes.  Cool in pan thoroughly before cutting.

In a large saucepan (used 6-qt. for doubled recipe), combine broth, undrained tomatoes, apple, carrot, celery, rice*, onion, raisins, sugar, curry powder, pepper, and mace.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 20 minutes or until rice is tender.  Stir in chicken; heat through.  Stir in cilantro.  Makes about 8 cups, or 4 servings.*
Combine spinach, onions, pepper, and margarine; spread in a 10”casserole.
To make the vinaigrette, place the pomegranate juice in a small pan and reduce to 2 tbsp. over medium-high heat.

Soak apricots, prunes and peaches in hot water for about 1 hour and then drain.  Cut fruit into pieces.  Beat eggs, add oil and then sugar.  Add cake meal.  Mix thoroughly.  Add fruit.  With wooden spoon mix thoroughly.  Turn into greased 9" x 12" baking pan.  Sprinkle with cinnamon.  Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until browned on top.  Serve with meat or fowl or as a dessert.
Can be prepared in advance, then baked later.
Combine the juice and the remaining vinaigrette ingredients in a small glass jar and shake vigorously to combine.
Place the mixed greens in a large bowl and add half of the vinaigrette, tossing to coat the leaves.  Add more dressing as desired.
Meanwhile, warm 1½ cups chocolate chips and sweetened condensed milk in small, heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.  Stir in vanilla.  Spread over hot crust.
_Note:_  I made 1½ times the recipe and baked it in a 9" x 13" pan.
Divide the salad between 4 chilled plates and decoratively arrange slices of persimmons or pears atop the greens.
In heavy saucepan, melt 1 cup chocolate chips with butter, stirring constantly.  Cool slightly.

Beat egg with sugars and vanilla until creamed.  Mix in melted chocolate.  Stir flour with baking soda, baking powder and salt.  Combine milk with lemon juice, stirring until thick.  Add dry ingredients to chocolate mixture alternately with milk.  Stir in remaining cup chocolate chips and cranberries.  Chill dough.
Drop by tablespoon onto ungreased baking sheet.  Bake at 350° for 8 – 10 minutes.  (I did 8 minutes.)  Cool on rack.  Makes about 5 dozen cookies.
Freezes well.
Bake pie crust according to package directions.  Cool.

Put the semisweet chocolate, unsweetened chocolate, and butter in the top of a double boiler over barely simmering water.  Stir together until melted.  Remove from over the water and set aside to cool slightly.

Put the eggs in a large bowl and mix on low speed just to blend the yolks and whites together.  Add the sugar, coffee, vanilla, and rum and beat for 2 minutes.  Add the chocolate mixture and beat just until the chocolate and eggs are mixed together completely.  Mix in the whipping cream.
Bake at 325° until top is browned, ~30 minutes.

Slowly pour the filling into the pie crust.  The filling will come up to the top of the pie crust.  Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.  The pie will look crackly on the top and feel soft, but it will firm as it cools.  (If using deep-dish 9" crust, may need to bake a few more minutes.)  Cool thoroughly.

To freeze for later use, wrap tightly with plastic wrap, then heavy aluminum foil.  To serve, defrost the covered pie at room temperature or in the refrigerator for 6 hours.  Serve at room temperature or chilled.  The chocolate will have a more intense taste at room temp.  Serve with whipped cream.  Store leftover pie in the frig.

Beat butter in large bowl until creamy.  Beat in flour, sugar, and salt until crumbly.  (Used pastry blender to help.)  With floured fingers, press 2 cups crumb mixture into bottom of greased 13" x 9" baking pan; reserve remaining mixture.  Bake at 350° for 10-12 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Stir until thick as marmalade.

Stir nuts and remaining chocolate chips into reserved crumb mixture; sprinkle over fudge filling.  Bake at 350° for 25-30 minutes or until center is set.  Cool in pan on wire rack; cut into squares.  Makes ~30 squares.
For the vinaigrette, in a small saucepan combine currant jelly and vinegar.  Cook and stir over medium-low heat just till jelly melts and mixture is smooth.  Chill in the freezer for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large salad bowl combine spinach, strawberries, orange sections, and green onion.  Drizzle vinaigrette over the spinach mixture; toss to mix.  Sprinkle with almonds and cheese and toss gently.  Serve immediately.  Serves 6-8.

Bring water to boil in saucepan and add wild rice.  Stir, cover, and simmer about 35 minutes or until just tender (took longer—check package instructions).  Drain excess liquid and transfer to large bowl.

Boil pineapple juice in 2nd saucepan and add basmati rice.  Stir, cover, and simmer 20 minutes (took much longer—check package instructions).  Liquid should be totally absorbed and rice tender.  Add to wild rice.
Heat oil in skillet and sauté onions, garlic, and mushrooms until soft.  Combine with rice mixture.  (Stop here if preparing in advance.)
Stir in remaining ingredients.  Transfer to greased 8" square baking pan.  Cover and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.

Heat oven to 350°F. Place shells onto ungreased baking sheet.  Combine mushrooms and hoisin sauce in small bowl.  Place 1 cube cheese in each shell.  Spoon mushroom mixture evenly into shells; sprinkle with shredded cheese.  Bake for 5 to 8 minutes or until heated through.  Remove immediately.  Serve warm.

TIP: To make ahead, prepare as directed except do not bake.  Layer between sheets of waxed paper in a resealable plastic freezer container; freeze.  At serving time, heat oven to 350°F. Place desired number of pastry cups onto ungreased baking sheet.  Bake for 12 to 20 minutes or until filling is hot.  Serve warm.
_For the Cake:_

Butter a 10" diameter springform pan.  Line bottom with waxed paper.  Stir butter and chocolate in heavy large saucepan over low heat until melted.  Mix sugar and cocoa in large bowl.  Add eggs; whisk until well blended.  Whisk in chocolate-butter mixture.  Pour batter into prepared pan.  Bake at 350° until tester inserted into center comes out clean, about 40-45 minutes.

Cool cake completely in pan on rack.  Run knife around pan sides to loosen cake.  Release pan sides.  Can be made 1 day ahead.  Cover and refrigerate.  Invert cake onto platter.  Glaze with recipe below. Freezes well.
_For the Chocolate Glaze:_

Melt butter in small saucepan over low heat.  Add cocoa and water; stir constantly until mixture thickens.  Do not boil.  Remove from heat; add vanilla.  Gradually add sugar, beating with a whisk until smooth.
To glaze cake, spread glaze around sides of cake.  Pour remaining glaze on top of cake and quickly and gently spread around.  It will set with a smooth surface.

Preheat broiler.  Combine mustard and dressing; stir well.  Arrange fish, skin side down, on a foil-lined baking sheet coated with no-stick cooking spray.  Brush half of mustard mixture over fish.  Broil fish for 8 minutes or until done.

While fish is cooking, combine onions and remaining mustard mixture in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.  Cover and cook 2 minutes.  Add half of spinach; cover and cook 1 minute or until it wilts.  Add remaining spinach and tomatoes and cook again for 1 minute.  Serve fish over spinach and tomatoes.

Using a large bowl, pour some boiling water over matzo just enough to absorb.  Let sit for 5 minutes, stirring a bit so all is absorbed.  (If there is excess water, drain it.)  Add milk, stirring it in, and let stand 5 minutes.  Mix in eggs; season.
Heat butter in 2 extra-large skillets.  Add matzo mixture.  Fry until golden on both sides.  Serve with maple syrup, cinnamon sugar, preserves, fresh or marinated fruit, etc.
Combine butter, cheeses, garlic, shallot, and vermouth in food processor with metal blade and process until smooth.  Season with hot pepper sauce.
Oil a 2-cup straight-sided mold, bowl, or pate´ terrine.  Line with plastic wrap.
Put layers of ingredients (cheese mixture, tomatoes, pesto, pine nuts) in the mold in any order.  Repeat until mold is full.

Fold plastic wrap over the top and press gently to compact the layers.  Chill until firm, at least 1 hour.  Invert onto platter, remove plastic, and serve with crackers and/or breads.  Serves a crowd.
Combine sauce ingredients in a non-metallic bowl.  Add chicken and toss to coat each piece well.  Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Place chicken on wire rack set over baking pan.  Bake at 350° until chicken is well browned and cooked through, 35 minutes.  Turn once during cooking.

Note:  I tripled sauce recipe (doubled ginger) and used 8 lbs. of wings (weight without tips).  Brushed wings with some sauce to marinate.  Brushed again before baking, again before and after turning, and once more at end.  Still had leftover sauce.  (This was about 70 pieces.)  Brushed leftover sauce on shrimp another day.
Place apricots and 1 cup Grand Marnier in saucepan.  Heat to boiling.  Remove from heat and set aside.
Sprinkle each serving with walnuts and pomegranate seeds and serve immediately.

Remove casing from sausage and cut into small pieces.  Cook in same skillet, breaking it up.  Cook until done.  Remove from heat and add to celery mixture.  Add stuffing mix, apricots with liquid, and almonds.  Stir to combine.
_To stuff turkey:_
Serve hot with crackers and/or baguette slices.

Rinse 18-22 lb. turkey and pat dry. Squeeze juice from 2 oranges and use baster to sprinkle over turkey and cavities. Spoon stuffing into cavities and sew or skewer shut. Put remaining stuffing in shallow dish.
Sprinkle turkey with thyme and pepper and brush with melted margarine. Then follow turkey baking instructions.
To bake extra stuffing, cover with foil and refrigerate when made. Then remove from frig. 30 minutes before baking. Bake ~1 hour at 350˚.
Bake at 425° for 10-12 minutes or until prosciutto is crisp.  Brush with glaze and serve warm.  Makes 16.
Butter and flour a 9" square pan.
Melt chocolate and butter in a double boiler over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth.  Remove from heat and cool.
_Filling - No cook method:_

In a bowl with an electric mixer, beat the eggs, sugar, and vanilla at high speed until light and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.  Blend in the cooled chocolate mixture at low speed.  Sift in the flour, 2 tbsp. of the cocoa, baking powder, and salt.  Mix on low speed to combine, stopping once or twice to scrape the sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula.

Fold in the raspberries with a rubber spatula, then scrape the batter into the prepared baking pan.  Bake at 325° for 40 to 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with some crumbs adhering to it.
Cool in the pan on a wire rack.  Cut into 16 squares and sprinkle with remaining 2 tsp. cocoa.  Can also sprinkle lightly with confectioner’s sugar on top of cocoa.
_Caramel Sauce:_ Whisk brown sugar and butter in heavy saucepan.  Whisk in cream and stir until sugar is dissolved and sauce is smooth, ~3 minutes.
For glaze, in a small saucepan, bring vinegar to a boil over medium heat; cook until reduced to about ¼ cup.  ~45 minutes.  (It was a lot of glaze.  Could probably make half this amount.)
In a food processor, combine all ingredients.  Mix well, but make sure that you don’t puree everything.  You still want some small pieces to add to the flavor and texture.  Makes about ¾ cup.

In a 4-qt. pot combine broth, vinegar, soy sauce, ginger, sugar, and pepper.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, for 2 min.  Add mushrooms.  Return to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, for 2 min. more.  Add tofu, bamboo shoots, and water chestnuts.*  Return to boiling.
Combine all ingredients except parsley and paprika.

_For topping:_ In a food processor, chop the nuts with the ginger until coarsely chopped.  Whiz in the flour, sugar, and cinnamon.  Pulse in the butter, leaving some chunks.  Add in the oats with just a couple of pulses.  Chill while preparing filling.  Can be made 1 day ahead.  Cover and keep chilled.
_For filling:_  Whisk first 3 ingredients in large bowl.  Add pears; toss.  Transfer to 13 x 9 x 2-inch oval baking dish.  Sprinkle topping over pear mixture.
Bake at 350° until topping is crisp and golden brown and juices are bubbling, about 50 minutes.  Serve warm.  Can top with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.
Note: I halved recipe and baked in 8" x 8" square baking dish.  Served 8-10.
Boil water in a pot.  Add eggs with a slotted spoon.  Add 1 tbsp. white vinegar.  Boil 20-25 min.  Strain.  Put in bowl and fill with cold water.  Replace cold water as needed.  Peel when cooled.
Bake in a well-greased cast iron skillet (used 12") at 350° for one hour.  Garnish with parsley and paprika.
I have also quickly cooked 1½ cups of shrimp and cut them into pieces to use in place of crab.
Heat 2 teaspoons olive oil in a large nonstick skillet set over medium-high heat.  Add the white sections of the green onion and ginger.  Cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Add the remaining 2 teaspoons olive oil to the skillet.  Add the crimini and shiitake mushrooms.  Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms just start to brown, 7 to 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and ground pepper and cook for 30 seconds.
While the mushrooms are cooking, whisk together the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, honey, and chili garlic sauce.
Pour the hoisin mixture into the skillet with the mushrooms and cook for 1 minute.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
In a large bowl, beat butter and sugar (with an electric mixer on medium speed or by hand) until light and fluffy.  Beat in eggs, vanilla, and milk.
In a small bowl, combine flour, oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.  Add to butter mixture and beat until blended.  Stir in remaining ingredients.
Remove from the heat and stir in the green sections of the green onions and the parsley.
Put the butter and two sugars into a mixing bowl.  Blend until well mixed.
Add the vanilla and mix.
Add the eggs, one at a time, blending thoroughly after each addition.
Stir the self-rising flour into the mixture.
Pour the chocolate chips in and mix.
Fill each mini fillo shell with 1 tablespoon of the mushroom mixture. Serve.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until it is golden brown and smells heavenly.

While still warm sprinkle with confectioner's sugar, then make 8 or 9 long cuts with a knife down the length of the cookie bar and  5 long cuts across the width, then allow the bars to cool in the  pan.
Heat oven to 400˚F. Line a cookie sheet with foil. Optionally, place a wire rack on the cookie sheet. Spray the rack or foil-covered sheet.

In a large bowl, mix all ingredients. Shape mixture into 24 (1.5 in) meatballs. Place about 1 inch apart on the rack or pan. To ensure even cooking, make all the balls the same size. One tip is to continually break the meat mixture into halves until you get down to the right size, then roll into balls (for 24, break in half (12), half (6), half (3), then form three even balls from what remains, and repeat).
Bake uncovered 18-22 minutes (less for extra lean meat) until temperature reaches 160˚F and no longer pink in the center.

Remove the casings from the sausage and break up into small chunks. Coat a saute pan with 1-2 tbsp olive oil then add the sausage and cook over medium heat. Gently brown the sausage and continue to break it up into smaller pieces (a potato masher works really well!). Optionally, sprinkle a dash or two of salt over the sausage as it cooks.
Mix all ingredients except potatoes in a small bowl.*

Once the sausage is browned on all sides (~5 minutes), lower the heat and add the cream, then top with some fresh cracked black pepper. Cook on low to medium-low for about 10 minutes, stirring often. You'll want the heat to be enough to create tiny bubbles in order to reduce and thicken the sauce, but be careful not to use too high of a heat that the cream boils or even curdles. As you're cooking, the cream and the oil may separate and have more of an orange color, especially early on. This is ok, as long as you stir enough as the sauce thickens that it eventually combines and emulsifies properly.
_Glaze:_  Whisk jelly and Kirsch together over medium heat until smooth.

Season meat with garlic powder and pepper and place fat-side up in a large pan. If using 6+ lbs. cut in half if possible. (Always use one recipe per pan, even if using two briskets (or two halves) in one pan.)

Finely chop your chosen fresh herbs. The amount and variety of herbs you choose are up to your taste. We used 4 sage leaves, 2-3 sprigs of thyme and 2-3 "branches" of rosemary (by "branches" I mean pieces that go out from the center "trunk" of a rosemary sprig, not 2-3 full sprigs), all removed from their stems. Add the chopped herbs and, if using, a whole bay leaf to the cream sauce and continue to cook, stirring often. The sauce is ready when it is no longer thin and liquidy but has thickened and is fully emulsified with the oil.
Brush on salmon.   If using steaks, brush on both sides.
Place salmon in a baking dish and bake at 425° for 10 minutes.
Optional:  Place under broiler and brown before serving.
Soak apricots, prunes, and peaches in hot water for 1 hour; drain.
Cut fruit into pieces.
Beat eggs, add oil, then sugar, then cake meal.
Mix thoroughly.  Add fruit with a wooden spoon and mix thoroughly.
Turn into greased 9" x 12" baking pan.  Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until browned on top.*
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into a 9" casserole dish.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes.
You may want to let it set a bit before serving.
Sauté mushrooms in a non-stick skillet sprayed with cooking spray until mushrooms are brown; drain.

While the sauce is cooking, boil water and cook the pasta according to the directions. With a slotted spoon, remove the cooked pasta from the water and place directly into the sauce. Toss to combine. Remove the pan from the heat, and stir in the freshly grated parmesan. Add in batches for best results.
Plate and serve immediately.

Grate the onion and potatoes. I use a food processor with the standard shredding disc and grate the potatoes and onions together. You can also use a box grater and grate them by hand, but it will take longer and require more overall effort.

As you complete batches of grating, squeeze all the excess moisture out over a large bowl (you will want to reserve the potato starch for binding). This step is super important! Do not be lazy! The best method we've found so far is to wrap the grated potatoes in cheese cloth and squeeze. The cheese cloth will help keep the liquid from reabsorbing as soon as you let go.

Once all of the potatoes and onions are grated and squeezed, carefully pour out the liquid that you squeezed out of the potatoes. You should see the separated potato starch at the bottom. In another large mixing bowl, combine potatoes, onions, eggs and potato starch. Stir with a fork. Add the rice flour, salt and pepper and stir to combine.
Fry for 2-3 minutes on each side or until golden brown. Transfer to a platter covered with paper towels and serve at once.

If you are making for a large crowd and want to serve all the latkes at once, preheat the oven to 225˚ F. Line a baking sheet with paper towels and place each latke in the warm oven as it comes off the stove.
Serve latkes with applesauce, sour cream, or other desired accompaniments.
Preheat the oven to 400° F.
Wash the Brussels sprouts then trim the stems and cut the Brussels sprouts in half.*
Add the sprouts and mushrooms to a large bowl. Drizzle with the olive oil and season with the garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place the Brussels sprouts and mushrooms on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until the Brussels sprouts are tender when pierced with a knife.
If desired, sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Spray a 13" x 9" baking dish with cooking spray.  Cut 20 one-inch slices from baguette* and arrange in one layer in baking dish.
Chill, covered, until all liquid is absorbed by bread, at least 8 hours, and up to 1 day.  Turn bread over a few times during this period, being sure to moisten the crusts, to help the liquid absorb.
Melt 1 tsp. butter in a small pot.  Toss pecans in and coat completely, adding salt.

Add olive oil to large saucepan and heat over medium heat. Add chopped onions to the pan. Sweat the onions for 2-3 minutes, then add the pancetta. Allow the pancetta to cook until most or all of the fat is melted off or crisped, then add half of the vodka. The vodka should bubble and cook off the alcohol.

Once you no longer smell alcohol in the pan, add the tomato passata. Add salt and pepper to taste. Maintain a simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens. This is the longest step, which should take 10-15 minutes if not longer. Keep a watchful eye and adjust the heat as needed to maintain a decent simmer without burning.
While the sauce is reducing, boil water and cook pasta according to package directions.

Once the sauce has thickened to a nice consistency, stir in the cream. Continue to maintain a low simmer so the sauce continues to thicken, but be careful not to separate or curdle the cream. Continue to reduce until the sauce has a consistency a bit thicker than you would like the final sauce to be (3-5 minutes), then stir in the other half of the vodka. Unlike the first addition of the vodka, at this step we do not want to lose all the alcohol aroma. Lower the heat and allow sauce to come together, 1-3 minutes. Taste the sauce and season with additional salt or pepper to taste.
Remove the pan from heat, add the penne pasta to the pan and toss to coat. Serve immediately.
Heat canola oil in large skillet until shimmering. Add Brussels sprouts, salt and pepper. Cook over high heat without stirring until sprouts are browned – about 2 minutes.
Add butter and brown sugar over medium high heat. Stir occasionally until brown sugar is melted. Add maple syrup. Cook until sprouts are crisp tender.
Stir in cider vinegar. Add chestnuts and walnut oil. Cook until hot. Transfer sprouts and chestnuts into bowl.
Boil liquid over high heat until slightly thickened – about 2 minutes. Pour over Brussels sprouts and chestnuts. Serve and enjoy!
_Dough:_
If you have a food processor: In food processor, combine all dough ingredients except butter and mix. Cut cold butter into pieces and add to other ingredients; mix.
By hand:  Cream softened butter and sugar.  Add egg and vanilla.  Sift flour and baking powder and stir into butter mixture.

Working in batches, drop a scant ¼ cup of potato mixture into the hot oil. (The latke mixture should sizzle when it hits the oil.) Using a fork or spatula, flatten the mixture a little in the pan. I fry 3-4 latkes at a time. This will ensure your oil doesn't get cold. Cold oil=greasy latkes!
In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, nutmeg, vanilla, and ¾ c. brown sugar and pour evenly over bread.
Cook 1 lb. dried apricots with water and some sugar to taste over gentle heat; cut apricots.  Add ¾ c. raisins (light or dark), few grains salt, and ¾ tsp. grated lemon rind.
Heat ⅛-inch of oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers but does not smoke.
Instead of cooking the fruits, you can put them in jars filled with water.  When they are soft, chop them to desired consistency in the food processor and add the remaining ingredients.
_Assembly:_
Roll dough out and cut into circles.  (Myra uses a 3" round cookie cutter.)  Place a small amount of filling in center of each circle.  Pinch dough together to make a triangle.
Bake at 375°, checking after 20 minutes.  Will probably need more time.
In a small saucepan, reduce the amaretto to ½ cup over medium-high heat.
Take a slice of apple and cheese and wrap a half slice of prosciutto around it. Repeat with remaining apple, cheese slices, and prosciutto.
Can double and cook in 11" x 14" pan.

Grease a 10" x 15" x 1" jelly roll pan and line with parchment paper.  Melt butter and herbs in a large skillet.  Gently cook mushrooms 5-7 minutes, until softened.  Add flour and bring to a boil, stirring constantly until thick.  Remove from heat and cool slightly.

In a medium bowl, beat egg whites until stiff.  Beat egg yolks into mushroom mixture, then fold in beaten egg whites and 2 tbsp. of chopped parsley.  Pour into prepared pan and bake at 400° for 12-15 minutes.  Cool.

In a small bowl, beat Boursin cheese, cottage cheese and chives.  Sprinkle a sheet of parchment paper with remaining parsley and Parmesan cheese.  Turn savory cake out onto parchment paper and spread with cheese mixture.  Cover with a layer of salmon if using.  Roll up, jelly roll style.  (Rolled along the long side into a 15" long roll.)

Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat.  Place the wrapped apples in the skillet cut side down and cook until the prosciutto is golden and crispy and the cheese is slightly melted, about 2-3 minutes per side.*

Place cocktail ryes on cookie sheet in single layer. Carefully place corned beef on each slice of rye. Add 1 tablespoon sauerkraut on top of corned beef. Place a dollop of thousand island dressing on top of sauerkraut. Top with Swiss cheese.  Can cover and refrigerate at this point if you want.
Serve warm, drizzling with honey just before serving.
To serve, cut into ½ - ¾ inch slices.
Makes enough for ¾ pound of chicken or fish.

Grate zest from 1 lime.  Squeeze juice from both limes to measure about ⅓ cup.  In a bowl, stir juice with zest, honey, and mustard until smooth (a whisk helps).  Brush fish with lime sauce.  Grill (or broil), basting often, until done, about 5 minutes per side (3 for tuna).
Preheat oven to 350˚. Just before serving, slide cookie sheet into oven for 5-8 minutes -- just until cheese has melted.

Whisk the eggs in a medium-sized bowl (used electric beater).  Break the matzoh into small pieces and add to the eggs.  Allow it to sit for a while, tossing occasionally, so the eggs soak in and soften the matzoh.
Add the goat cheese, spooning it into the mixture in small bits.  Stir in the figs.
Melt the butter in a skillet (used 10").  Add the egg mixture, sprinkle with pepper, and scramble until cooked, about 2 minutes.  Can serve with maple syrup.
_Alternatives:_
Replace figs and goat cheese with:
•	tomatoes and feta
•	cheddar and broccoli
•	provolone and spinach
Using a food processor or blender, puree mango, chili sauce, and oil until smooth.  Season to taste with ground pepper.
Good with crab cakes.
Can be made a day ahead and refrigerated.  Bring to room temperature before serving.
Combine the mango, sour cherries, dried cherries, nutmeg and cinnamon in a bowl.  Pour hot amaretto over the fruit and stir with a spoon to coat evenly.  Set aside to macerate for 30 minutes.
Chop macaroons and almonds in food processor.  Add butter and pulse until combined but still crumbly.
Butter a 10" ovenproof pan (used oval white quiche dish).  Spoon the fruit and accumulated juices into the pan.
If preparing in advance, cover pan.  Place crumb topping in separate container and refrigerate both.  Bring baking dish to room temperature before proceeding.
Scatter macaroon mixture evenly over the top of the fruit.  Bake at 375° for 25 – 35 minutes or until the fruit is bubbling and the top is golden brown.  Serve warm.

Mix crumbs and butter.  Press onto bottom of 8" or 9" square pan.  (Can line pan with foil, leaving overhang on all sides.  This makes is easy to lift the finished cake out of the pan for easier cutting.)
Mix cream cheese, sugar and vanilla with electric mixer on medium speed until well blended.  Add eggs; mix until blended.  Pour over crust.
Place potatoes in a lightly greased 13” x 9” x 2” baking pan or a shallow baking sheet; toss with mustard mixture.
Bake at 350° for 35-40 minutes or until center is almost set.  Run knife around rim of pan to loosen cake.  Cool; refrigerate 3 hours or overnight.  Cut into squares or rectangles.
Can top with sliced strawberries.
Used salmon fillet and baked at 400° for about 12 minutes.  Needed to turn it near the end.
In a small bowl, stir together all ingredients.  Brush evenly onto chicken or fish.  Refrigerate 30 minutes.  Grill.
Adjust an oven rack to the lowest shelf and preheat oven to 350°.

Mix the granulated sugar, the remaining 3 tbsp. flour, and salt in a small saucepan.  Whisk in the milk, egg yolks, lemon juice, and lemon zest.  Cook the mixture over medium heat, stirring, until it thickens, 5-7 minutes.  Remove the pan from the heat, then stir in the strawberries.  Cool slightly on a rack.

Spread the cooled custard over the crust.  Bake until the custard is set, about 30 minutes.  Remove the pan from the oven and let cool on a rack.  Dust with confectioners’ sugar and cut into 16 squares.  Cover and store in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

In a small bowl, stir together flour, baking powder, and salt.  In a medium bowl, with electric mixer on medium speed, beat egg whites until foamy.  Gradually beat in ¼ c. granulated sugar.  Increase mixer speed to medium-high and beat until stiff and glossy peaks form.

In a large bowl, combine remaining 2 tbsp. light butter, remaining ¼  c. granulated sugar, the egg yolk, and vanilla.  With electric mixer on medium speed, beat until blended, about 2 minutes.  Beat in half the milk.  Reduce mixer sped to low and beat in half the flour mixture.  Beat in remaining milk, the orange zest, and then remaining flour mixture.  Stir in spoonful of beaten egg whites to lighten mixture.  Gently fold in remaining whites in 2 additions, just until blended.  Pour batter evenly over pears in skillet.

_Make Cream Sauce:_  Melt butter in a non-stick pan.  Whisk in flour.  Stir over low heat until bubbly.  Slowly whisk in hot milk, and stir over medium heat until bubbly and thick.   Boil 1 minute.  Add white pepper to taste.
In a double boiler, scramble eggs, but leave moist.  Mix in Cream Sauce.  Divide between 4 greased ramekins.

Spread 2 tablespoons sour cream per ramekin.  Crumble 3 strips bacon per ramekin (or shrimp) as the third layer.  Can add layers of diced seeded tomatoes, artichoke hearts, maybe mushrooms.  Top each with 1 tablespoon each type of cheese.  I sprinkled extra cheese on each.
Bake at 350° for 15 – 20 minutes  (Baked 20 minutes.)

Season lamb with salt and pepper.  In a 4-quart pot, brown meat, half at a time, in hot oil over medium-high heat.  Drain fat.  Return all meat to pan.  Sprinkle meat with flour, stirring to coat.  Add broth, nectar, cinnamon, garlic, cumin, cardamom, and saffron; stir to combine.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, for 1 hour or until meat is nearly tender.

Add carrots, onions, apricots, and prunes.  Return to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 30 minutes more or until vegetables are tender.  Remove stick cinnamon (if using).  Serve over Mashed Sweet Potatoes.
_Mashed Sweet Potatoes:_

In a large saucepan cook sweet potatoes, covered, in a moderate amount of lightly salted boiling water for 20 – 25 minutes or until tender; drain.  Mash with a potato masher or beat with an electric mixer on low speed.  Add butter and yogurt; mash or beat.

In a small bowl stir together hoisin sauce, five-spice powder, and enough orange juice (1 to 2 tbsp.) to thin mixture for brushing.  Brush evenly onto meat or fish during last 5 minutes of grilling or broiling.  Makes enough for 2 pounds of poultry or fish.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes or until golden and bubbly.  Can be served topped with vanilla ice cream.
Can be made several hours in advance and left at room temperature.  Heat at 200° for 10 minutes before serving.
_Crust:_  Crush cookies with berries in food processor until both are finely ground.  Add butter and process to combine.  Press into bottom and up sides of a 10" tart pan.  Chill.
_Topping:_  In a small bowl, combine flour and sugar; cut in butter until crumbly.  Stir in almonds.

Preheat oven to 425°F and place a large baking sheet in middle of oven.  Spoon filling into tart shell, smoothing top.  Sprinkle topping over filling.  Bake tart on preheated baking sheet in middle of oven until done.  Check after 30 minutes.  (I baked it 40 minutes.)  Cool tart in pan on a rack at least 1 hour.
Tart may be made 1 day ahead and kept, covered, at room temperature.
_Note:_ There was a lot of filling, so I mounded it high.  For a more typical tart you could probably make half to three-quarters the filling recipe.

Place challah in a greased 9" x 13" baking dish and top with Nova, cheese, and chives.  Combine eggs and remaining ingredients and pour over Nova mixture.  Press ingredients down, to moisten thoroughly.  Cover and chill overnight.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 40 – 45 minutes or until set and edges are puffed and golden.  Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
_Variation:_

Halved recipe and baked in Cape May quiche dish.  Used 4 thick slices (~½ of a loaf) of Trader Joe’s French brioche instead of challah; ~12 cooked 50 – 60-count shrimp, cut up, instead of Nova; and Italian blend (6 cheeses) instead of Swiss.  Served 6.
Cut the Nova to fit on each cracker.  Stir a bit of curry powder, according to your taste, into the chutney.  Spoon chutney over Nova on each cracker.  Top each with a dollop of crème fraiche.

In a 10-inch cast-iron skillet or other heavy 10-inch ovenproof skillet, melt 1 tbsp. light butter over medium heat.  Brush melted butter to coat bottom and halfway up sides of skillet.  Remove from heat.  Sprinkle bottom evenly with brown sugar.  In bottom of skillet, arrange pear wedges, rounded side down, like spokes of a wheel, leaving center open.  Fill in center and spaces between pears with cranberries.
Brush warm glaze over berries, coating them evenly.  Refrigerate tart for 2 hours.  Remove from refrigerator 45 minutes before serving.
Combine the cheeses in a bowl and sprinkle with the flour. Toss to evenly coat, set aside.

Bake at 350° until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean, 35-40 minutes.  Transfer skillet to wire rack to cool for 3 minutes.  Invert serving plate over skillet.  Using mitts to protect your hands, carefully invert cake onto plate.  Remove skillet.  Spread any glaze remaining in skillet over pears.  Let cake cool completely.
Melt 6 oz. semisweet chocolate with bittersweet chocolate, 1 cup butter, sugar, and cream, stirring frequently until smooth.  Cool slightly and stir in vanilla.
Beat eggs at medium speed with electric mixer 1 minute.  Beat chocolate mixture into eggs until smooth.  Pour batter into pan and tap gently on work surface to break any large air bubbles.
Turn cake over onto cake plate.  If freezing, line plastic board with plastic wrap and turn cake onto board instead.  Remove pan and paper.

Melt remaining chocolate and butter, stirring until smooth for glaze.  Use a spatula to spread over sides, then pour over top and spread.  It will be runny but keep smoothing while it sets.  Clean excess glaze from plate/board.
In a bowl mix whipping cream and mustard.  Spoon mixture over egg yolks until coated.  Sprinkle with salt and red pepper.

If freezing, place board in freezer until cake is frozen.  Then run a thin sharp knife around bottom edges to loosen.  Bring up plastic and wrap tightly.  Remove board and return frozen cake to freezer.  To serve, remove plastic and place on serving platter.
In a jar with a tight lid, combine the vinegar, raspberry preserves, olive oil, and black pepper.  Add the cranberries.  Shake the container well to coat.  Let stand for 10 minutes.

Divide the salad greens between six plates.  Top each one with the shredded carrots, then the apples, then the fish.  Spoon the cranberries on top and sprinkle with the pistachios.  Drizzle the dressing over the top of each serving.
I doubled the recipe and served it on a large platter.  I tossed the salad greens with some of the dressing first, then made the layers, and drizzled more dressing over the top.  Served 12-15.
Lightly coat a 9" x 9" x 2" square baking pan with cooking spray.  (Used ceramic quiche dish—round in CM, oval in WW.)
_Make filling:_  In a large bowl toss filling ingredients.  Transfer to prepared baking pan.

_Make topping:_  In a medium bowl, stir together oats, flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt until no lumps of brown sugar remain.  In a small bowl, stir together oil and juice.  Drizzle juice mixture over oat mixture and toss until evenly moistened  and crumbly.  Press together small handfuls of oat mixture to  make streusel-like pieces and arrange on top of filling to cover.  Sprinkle evenly with almonds.
Bake at 375° until topping is browned and filling is bubbly, 40 – 45 minutes.  Cool slightly on wire rack.  Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
Lightly butter a 9" x 13" baking pan.
Combine all ingredients and pour over fish.

Meanwhile, combine the filling ingredients.  Spread on baked crust and sprinkle reserved crumbs and remaining almonds on top.  Bake 45-50 minutes until plums are bubbling around a golden topping.  Cut into squares.
Combine first 3 ingredients in a shaker with ice.  Strain into champagne flute.  Slowly add the sparkling wine, stirring gently.

Can also combine the first 3 ingredients in a pitcher, using equal parts of the first 3 ingredients.  Chill well.  To serve, stir well and pour mixture into champagne flute. Top with equal amount of sparkling wine.  Stir gently.

I mixed 2 cups each of the first 3 ingredients and shook mixture in a covered pitcher.  Poured half of the mixture into a punch bowl and slowly added a bottle (750 ml) of Prosecco.  Gently stirred and served with punch glasses.  When this was gone, I repeated with the other half of the mixture and another bottle of Prosecco.  Served at potluck dinner with 36 people and other beverages.
Cream the eggs and sugar using an electric hand mixer.  Add the oil and the pumpkin.  Mix the dry ingredients together in a small bowl and add in thirds, mixing well.  Fold in the chocolate chips.

Generously grease a bundt or tube pan with cooking spray.  Pour batter into pan.  Bake at 350° for 60-70 minutes until toothpick comes out clean.  Don't overbake.  (I checked at 60 min. and it was definitely done.  Used dark pan.  Maybe should reduce temperature or check it earlier, as it was only somewhat moist.)

Cool in the pan on a wire rack about 20 minutes.  Run a thin knife or spatula around the pan to make sure it doesn't stick to the sides or middle.  Turn out onto a cake plate.  Put a cake plate lid on it so the top stays moist instead of crisping up.
After it cools, it freezes beautifully.
If you want, you can drizzle with the following glaze:

In a small saucepan over low heat, blend chips, butter, and milk, stirring constantly until chips melt.  Remove from heat.  Stir in powdered sugar until smooth.  Add additional milk if necessary for glazing consistency.

Peel and coarsely chop vegetables.  Tie herbs together with string.  Add all to broth.  Slowly simmer, partially covered, for 45 minutes.  Strain out the solids.  Season with  pepper and salt, if needed.
If making matzo balls, use some of the broth to cook them.  Remove balls and strain broth.  Add remaining broth.
Spray 9" x 13" pan with cooking spray.  Combine first 7 ingredients in a large bowl.  Gently fold in bread cubes and raisins.  Cover and refrigerate overnight.

Remove dish from frig and bring to room temperature.  Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.  Let stand ~10 minutes; sprinkle with powdered sugar.  Can serve with maple syrup or Caramel Sauce (recipe follows).

Place pan into larger pan (used 10" x 14").  Pour water into larger pan, filling about ¾ of an inch up sides of cake pan to create water bath.  Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes until edges of cake are set but center is still soft.  Remove pan from water bath.  Cool.  Cake may sink a little in center and may crack slightly.

Combine egg, egg yolk, and vanilla.  Gradually add to dry mix, tossing with a fork and your fingers until mixture begins to come together.  Set ⅓ of mixture aside and press remainder into the prepared pan.  Prick all over with a fork, then refrigerate 15-20 minutes.  Bake at 350° for 18-20 minutes until lightly golden.  Set aside to cool.
Bake at 350° for ~20 minutes.*
_Crust:_ Preheat oven to 350°.  Mix ingredients with a food processor or a pastry blender until crumbly.  Press mixture evenly on the bottom of a 9x13-inch pan.  Bake for 12 to 15 minutes.

_Filling:_ Dissolve coffee in hot water.  Combine remaining filling ingredients with an electric mixer or food processor.  Stir in dissolved coffee.  Spread over baked crust.  Bake for 15 minutes, or until center is set.  Cool.

_Frosting:_ In a saucepan, melt butter.  Stir in cocoa and remove from heat.  Dissolve coffee in hot water.  Add to butter mixture and stir in confectioners’ sugar.  Beat until smooth with an electric mixer.  Spread over brownies.  Cool and cut into squares.
If using raw chicken, in a large saucepan cook chicken, half at a time, in hot butter over medium heat until no longer pink.  Remove chicken with a slotted spoon, reserving drippings in saucepan.

Add sweet potato, onion, Serrano peppers, coriander, and cumin to saucepan; add half of the chicken broth.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 20 minutes or until vegetables are very tender.  Cool slightly.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.  Watch carefully.  To serve, cut into "nests" and lift out.
Dish may be assembled and refrigerated the day before.  Bring to room temperature before baking.
Let set in pan, then cut in 2” squares.

Heat oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add onions and bell pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 5 minutes.  Add the garlic and ginger and cook for another minute. Add the curry powder and cumin, cook for a few more minutes. The spices will absorb some of the oil, so if anything begins to stick too much to the bottom of the pan, add a little more oil to the pan.

Add the vinegar, coconut milk, and one of the two chopped mangos to the pan. Increase the heat and bring to a boil, then lower the heat to maintain a low simmer for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Combine nuts and syrup.  Cut stem from each fig.  Using your finger (wear glove), push into stem opening and stretch to create hollow pocket.  Stuff with nut mixture.  Place in a hot oven or microwave until figs are just warmed.

Butter a shallow 2-quart casserole or 10" ovenproof pie pan.  (Used 10" square Corningware baking dish.)  In a medium bowl combine the flour, sugar, and cinnamon.  Cut in the butter until mixture is crumbly.  Mix in the oats.

Spread the fruit in the prepared baking dish (apples on bottom if using) and sprinkle topping over fruit.  (Can cover and refrigerate until later.)  Bake at 350° until the topping is browned and berries are bubbly, about 40 minutes.  Serve warm or at room temperature with ice cream or lightly sweetened whipped cream.

In a saucepan bring broth to boiling.  Add zucchini, green onion, ginger, lemongrass, and crushed red pepper.  Return to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, uncovered, for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add coconut milk and heat gently.  Add shrimp and heat through (do not boil) until shrimp turn pink.  Top with shredded basil.
Remove pan from heat. Scoop the sauce into a blender. Purée the sauce, pulsing until smooth. Return the sauce to the pan.
Add chicken and raisins (if using) to the pan and return to a low simmer. Cover the pan and let cook for 8 - 10 minutes. The chicken should be just cooked until done.

Add the remaining chopped mango.  Cook at a very low temperature for another minute or two, uncovered.  If a little too sweet, add a little more vinegar. If not sweet enough, you can add a dash of sugar. Add salt and pepper to taste.  Serve over rice or with Naan for dipping and garnish with cilantro, if desired.
Cut chicken into bite-size strips.*  In a 4-quart saucepan stir together chicken, broth, fish sauce, lemon juice, ginger, and cumin.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes.

Sir in broccoli, sweet pepper, jalapeno pepper, green onions, and cilantro.  Return to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 10 minutes more or until vegetables are tender.  Add coconut milk; heat through but do not boil.

In a small bowl combine the 1 tsp. sugar, the ⅛ tsp. nutmeg, and the ⅛ tsp. cinnamon.  Sprinkle over pear mixture.  Place dish in a 13x9x2-inch baking pan; set on oven rack.  Pour hot water in the 13x9x2-inch baking pan to a depth of 1 inch.  Bake in a 350° oven about 45 minutes or till a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.  Serve warm or cool.
Note:  You can halve this recipe for 1 average-sized mold.

_Crust:_  Combine the flour, salt, and brown sugar.  With a pastry blender or 2 knives, cut in the butter.  Stir in the chocolate and nuts.  Mix the vanilla and water and add to the crumbs.  Work the mixture with your hands to combine.  With floured fingers, push the mixture into a 9" or 10" false-bottom tart pan, covering the bottom and sides.  Bake at 350° for 20-25 minutes (baked 23 min. for 9" pan, 20 min. for 10" pan).  Cool completely.
_Filling:_  Melt chocolate in a double boiler.  Add melted butter and Kirsch.  Whisk quickly and thoroughly until smooth.  Add confectioners’ sugar and water, continuing to whisk until smooth.
Spread warm filling into tart shell.  Place berries, tips up, over the warm filling in a circular pattern, working from the outside in until the surface is covered.
Made ¼ of recipe with about ¾ pound shrimp.  Had extra marinade.

In a large mixing bowl beat cream cheese, the ⅔ c. sugar, lemon peel, vanilla, the ¼ tsp. nutmeg, and the ¼ tsp. cinnamon with an electric mixer on low speed till smooth.  Beat in eggs, 1 at a time, beating just till combined after each addition.  With a large spoon, stir in milk, half-and-half, or light cream; bread; pears; and chocolate pieces.  Pour mixture into an ungreased 2-qt. square baking dish, stirring gently to distribute chocolate pieces.
Pour cooking wine and garlic into a pot and cook over medium-high heat. Once it starts to boil add the spinach and artichokes, stir until the spinach wilts.
Stir in the cheeses and keep stirring until the cheese is stringy and melted completely. Transfer to a fondue pot, or keep in pot on low heat until ready to serve.
Serve with your choice of dipping ingredients.

Spray a 13" x 9" x 2" baking dish with cooking spray.  Arrange broccoli and half of green onions evenly over bottom of dish.  Sprinkle with salmon, Swiss cheese, cream cheese, and remaining half of green onions.
Mix eggs, milk, baking mix, and pepper in blender until smooth.  Pour batter over salmon mixture.  Bake at 375° until just set in center, about 45 – 55 minutes.  Let cool 10 minutes before serving.

To prepare a day in advance:  Complete first paragraph above.  Cover and refrigerate.  Combine remaining ingredients except baking mix in blender jar and refrigerate.  To bake, remove baking dish and blender jar from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.  Add baking mix to blender and continue as above.
Peel shrimp, leaving tails intact.  Devein shrimp, if desired.
Toss together shrimp, chili powder, salt, and olive oil in a large bowl.  Thread 5 shrimp onto each skewer, bending each shrimp to pass through skewer twice.
_Curried Mango Sauce:_ Process all ingredients in a blender until smooth, stopping once to scrape down sides.  Makes 1 cup.
Bake at 425° for 35 - 40 minutes or until potatoes are fork tender, stirring occasionally.

Grill, without grill lid, over high heat (400° to 500°) 4 to 5 minutes or just until shrimp turn pink, turning once.  Serve warm with Curried Mango Sauce.  Garnish with lime wedges.  Serves 6 as an entrée, 8-10 as an hors d’oeuvre.
I tried to make nest shapes, but the cheese spread out while baking.  However, it was easy to cut each "nest" and lift out of the dish.

In a covered saucepan, sauté the onions and apples in the oil for ~10 minutes, until the onions are translucent.  Sprinkle in the flour and cook, stirring, for a minute or two.  Then stir in the stock, lemon juice and peel, curry powder, dill, white pepper, and wine.  Simmer, covered, for ~5 minutes, until the mixture thickens slightly.  Add the half-and-half.

Remove lemon peel.  In a food processor or blender, puree the soup and then return to the pot.  Add the shrimp and simmer gently just until the shrimp turn pink.  Be careful not to overcook the shrimp or they will become tough.  Serves 4 as a main dish, 6 as a first course.

In a large saucepan (used 4-qt.) combine the broth, wine, cilantro, lemon zest, and pepper.  Bring to boiling.  Add scallops (if using), asparagus, shiitake mushrooms (if using), and green onions.  Return to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, uncovered, for 3 minutes.  Add shrimp (if using).  Simmer 2 minutes or until asparagus is tender and seafood is opaque.
Remove saucepan from heat.  Stir in the enoki mushrooms (if using) and lemon juice.
Pour all the ingredients into a cocktail shaker with ice cubes.  Shake well.  Strain into a highball glass.  Garnish with the orange slice.  Makes 1 serving.

Butter 6 ramekins and place a bread slice on the bottom of each.
Cover each with a slice of Swiss cheese, then a slice of ham or bacon.
Break an egg into each ramekin.
Arrange 3 halved cherry tomatoes (or 1 slice of regular tomato cut into 6 pieces) around each egg.  Sprinkle with seasonings.
Pour 2 tbsp. cream over each egg.  Sprinkle with grated Swiss cheese.
In a small bowl, mash the margarine, parsley, dill and salad dressing with a fork.  Set aside.
Toss the salmon and mushrooms with the lemon-pepper seasoning and garlic powder.
Bake at 350° for 15 - 20 minutes or until eggs set.
Cook sugar, butter, and syrup until syrupy.  Pour into a 9" x 13" baking dish.
Cover with all the apple slices.
Whisk together remaining ingredients and pour over bread.  Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake uncovered for 40 minutes at 350°.  Cut into squares and spoon sauce from bottom over.
Line the bowl with 2 strips of wax paper (criss-cross), long enough to have a generous overhang; brush with oil.
Combine fish,  egg, ice water, matzo meal, onion, horseradish, sugar, salt, and pepper; blend well.
Fold dill into remaining mixture.
Layer the carrot mixture on top.
Repeat with remaining dill mixture.
Cover with wax paper overhang.
Remove and turn out onto platter.  Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.*
Slice bread into ¾" slices, remove crusts all around, and place in a single layer on top of apple slices.  Squeeze to fit.
In a separate bowl, place ⅓ of fish mixture; fold in carrot.
Lightly oil a 1½-quart ovenproof bowl.

To assemble:  Spread half the margarine-herb mixture inside the bread shell, coating the bottom and sides.  Add the salmon and mushrooms, and spread evenly over the herb mixture.  Top with the remaining margarine-herb mixture, spreading over the filling.  Completely cover with a thick layer of breadcrumbs, pressing down with hands.  Spray crumbs with cooking spray.

Place on a baking sheet and bake at 400° for 45 minutes, until topping is deep brown.  (If the topping gets too dark, cover loosely with aluminum foil.)  Let the loaf rest for 10 minutes before cutting into thick slices.  Serves 6.

_Notes:_  I doubled recipe and used one 2-pound loaf of Tuscany bread (from Genuardi’s).  Cooked perfectly using above timing and served 10.  However, the thick crispy crust made slicing difficult.  Some possible solutions to try:
•	Cover crust with aluminum foil.  (Leave top exposed.)
•	Use a bread with a softer crust.  (The French bread called for in the recipe may have been less dense than Tuscany.)

In a skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat.  Add shallots and mushrooms and sauté for 5 minutes.  Add wine and sauté for 5 minutes longer or until shallots and mushrooms are soft and golden.  Remove from heat.

Scrub potatoes and place in large bowl.  Brush with olive oil.  Sprinkle with rosemary, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.  Toss in shallots and mushrooms and mix.  Place into 9" x 13" baking pan.  Drizzle with 3 tablespoons olive oil.
Cover dried cranberries with port and let sit overnight (or at least for a few hours).
Dice squash into small pieces; slice red onion.  Mix with olive oil and maple syrup, season with pepper and roast in a 400° oven for 25 – 35 minutes until squash is cooked and onions browned.
_Sherry Maple Vinaigrette:_ Combine vinegar, mustard, maple syrup, and shallots in a bowl (I used mini-prep food processor). Slowly whisk in oil.  Season with pepper.

Toss greens with some vinaigrette and arrange on plates or a large platter. Top each plate of greens with squash and onions.  Drain cranberries and sprinkle them and pecans on top.  Garnish with goat cheese and drizzle more vinaigrette.
All parts can be prepared the day before.  Bring to room temperature and assemble just before serving.

On 2 large rimmed baking sheets, toss the brussels sprouts with the oil and season with pepper.  Roast at 400° for 30-40 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sprouts are tender and browned in spots.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, combine the cranberries, maple syrup, ginger and orange zest.  Cook over moderately low heat, stirring, until the cranberries break down and thicken, about 10 minutes.

In a medium skillet, cook the butter over moderately high heat until deep golden, about 4 minutes.  Remove from the heat, add the shallot and thyme and stir into the cranberry sauce.  Transfer the butter to a bowl; add the brussels sprouts and toss.
Note:  The cranberry brown butter can be refrigerated for up to 3 days.  Gently reheat the butter before tossing with the brussels sprouts.
Butter a 3-quart casserole.  Line with cheese.  Make a well (the nest) in the cheese to hold each egg.  Break eggs into nests.
Serve hot or cold.

Remove from oven. Remove meat from pan and allow to cool ~1 hour. Can return pan to the oven on warm to keep the gravy warm while the meat cools. Once cool enough, slice. Return pieces to the warm gravy in the pan as you slice it. Serve once sliced!
_Tips_
Can make ahead, slice and freeze, then defrost in the frig. for 24 hours, then heat with loosely covered foil at 300˚-325˚ for 30-45 minutes until warm.

Can make a day in advance, slice, then cover with saran wrap and refrigerate. To reheat, you can microwave for 9 minutes (3 x 3 minutes, stirring in between) and/or put in warm over (200˚-250˚) covered loosely with foil for an hour before serving.
For faster cooking, you can raise the temperature (4-5 hours on 325˚, less at 350˚) but it's not recommended.
Place shrimp in a bowl.

In a saucepan, combine the apricots, cranberries, cherries (or raisins), ginger, ⅓ cup of wine, and 1 tbsp. of the mint and mix well.  Place over medium heat and bring to a simmer.  Cover and cook for about 10 minutes, until the fruit softens.  (The fruit can be covered and refrigerated for up to 8 hours before using.)
Roast, uncovered, at 400°, stirring occasionally, for 1 to 1½ hours or until potatoes are soft when tested with a knife.

The recipe works with basically any size brisket. I've made it with a very small 2.5-3 lb. brisket as well as a full 12-13 lb. brisket. The key is to make one recipe of the sauce per pan, regardless of how much meat you use. If using a tiny brisket, just use a smaller pan. As long as there's roughly the same amount of empty space in the pan, you'll dilute with about the same amount of water, and it will all taste great.

Place a 12" cast iron skillet in the center of the oven and preheat oven to 425°.  Whisk together the eggs, milk, flour, and sugar (and vanilla, if using) until very frothy.  You can use an electric mixer or blender.

Remove the skillet from the oven and melt the butter in it, tilting the pan until the butter coats the bottom and sides of the pan.  Pour the batter into the skillet.  Place the skillet into the center of the oven and bake for about 15 minutes until the pancake is golden brown and puffed up.  Carefully remove from pan (it will fall as it cools) and serve immediately.
_Serve with any of the following_
Maple syrup
Cinnamon sugar
Fresh fruit and/or berries
Lemon curd
Nutella
Powdered sugar
Honey
Whipped cream
In a separate bowl, combine the next 6 ingredients.
Sprinkle mixture over shrimp and toss well.
Cover and refrigerate until needed.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Add peas and toss; sauté for a minute or 2.
Add shrimp and sauté until shrimp turn pink, ~2 minutes.
Add wine and orange juice and cook until almost all the liquid is absorbed.
Add mango and cook until it is just heated through, 1 minute more.
Remove pan from heat and stir in cilantro.
Sprinkle with coconut.
Preheat oven to 350°.  Grease a 9x9 inch casserole dish.  (Used 7x11 inch dish.)
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.  Set aside.
Sauté onion and mushrooms.  Set aside.
Beat eggs (used mixer).  Add all cheeses, butter, onion and mushrooms.  Mix well.
Add flour mixture.
Pour into casserole dish.
Place slices of tomato on top and push in slightly.  Sprinkle with parsley and any extra cheese.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Sauté garlic in oil briefly.
Add shrimp.  Cook on medium heat for one minute.
Add tomatoes, feta, lemon juice, and dill.  Stir so that the shrimp cook on both sides.
When the shrimp are pink and the tomatoes and feta have made a sauce, it's ready.
Sprinkle with pepper and serve at once over rice, couscous, or orzo.*
In a blender or food processor fitted with a metal blade, pulse/chop the matzah meal, thyme salt and pepper until the meal is powdery. Place in a shallow dish, set aside.
In another shallow bowl, whisk egg whites until light in color.
Dip chicken breast pieces in egg whites, then dredge in matzah meal.
Place in lightly oiled baking dish (9x12); lightly spray one side of breasts with oil and place in 400˚ over for 3 minutes. Remove from oven and turn oven down to 350˚.
In a large skillet, sauté onions and garlic in olive oil until the onions are translucent. Add mushrooms and sauté for 3 minutes. With a slotted spoon, remove mushrooms and spoon over breasts.
With remaining juices still in the skillet, return the skillet to the flame, pour in sherry, stock, orange juice and paprika. Simmer for 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in parsley.
Pour sauce over mushrooms and chicken. Cover and bake for 45 minutes.
Garnish with more parsley and serve.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a bowl.
Transfer to an 8½" x 5" baking dish.  Sprinkle with paprika.

In saucepan combine dried fruit bits, coconut, cinnamon, ½ c. red wine, and water.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Cover and simmer about 25 minutes or until the dried fruit is tender and liquid is absorbed.

Place half the fruit mixture in a food processor or blender.  Cover and process or blend until smooth.  Stir into remaining fruit mixture along with the 2 tbsp. wine.  Cover and store in frig. up to 2 weeks.
Before serving, stir in almonds, which have been toasted by placing in 350˚ oven for 10 minutes and stirring occasionally until golden.
Sprinkle ½ cup cheese over spinach.  Arrange mushrooms on top and season with garlic powder.  Cover with remaining cheese.
You can cover and refrigerate it until ready to bake.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.*
Fold in chocolate chips.

Cut leaves and stems from the beets, leaving about a ½-inch stem.  Snap off the "tail."  Wash the beets; leave wet.  Place in a microwave-safe bowl. Cover and microwave on high about 12 minutes, until beets are tender.  May want to rotate the beets after 5 minutes so that beets at outer edge of dish are moved to the center.  Drain and cool.

Meanwhile, add the sugar to the eggs and beat at high speed for 5 minutes until the mixture is almost white.  On lowest speed add the sifted dry ingredients, scraping the bowl with a rubber spatula and beating only until incorporated.  Using a large rubber spatula, fold in the liquid butter and then the vanilla.  Then fold in the coconut, then ½ cup of the chocolate chips, and finally the cranberries.

Combine flour, oats, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.  Beat butter and brown sugar in a large bowl until creamy.  Add eggs, flour mixture, ½ cup chocolate chunks, and ¼ cup cranberries; blend well.

Place apricots in medium saucepan and cover with nectar or juice and water.  Let stand 1 hour for fruit to soften.  Place over medium heat and simmer, uncovered, until apricots are very tender, about 30 minutes.  Cool and drain well, reserving liquid.

Lightly grease a 2-quart (7" x 11") shallow baking dish.  Arrange half of the potatoes in a layer in dish, then cover with a layer of half of the apricots.  Sprinkle with half the brown sugar.  Repeat layers.
At this point, the casserole can be covered and refrigerated before being baked, for up to 2 or 3 days.  Before baking, bring to room temp.

Bake uncovered at 350° for 50 minutes, basting occasionally with liquid in bottom of dish.  (Basting may be difficult, so don’t worry about it if you can’t.)  Remove from oven and place pecans on top.  Return to oven and bake until casserole is bubbling and top is well glazed, 5-10 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Press dough into a greased 10" x 15" x 1" pan.  Bake at temperature recommended on can for 8 minutes.  Remove from oven and cool.
Combine cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco in the bowl of a food processor and whiz for 30 seconds.
Place salmon all over pizza crust, tearing into pieces to fill.  Spread entire surface with cheese mixture.*  Sprinkle with tomatoes and herbs.
Bake at same temperature as before for 5 minutes.  Cut into squares and serve.  Makes 12-20 pieces.

Unroll the dough. Arrange in a greased 9- to 9½-inch quiche dish or a 9-inch pie plate.  Seal all of the seams, tearing pieces to fill in the holes.

Remove any cartilage from crabmeat.  Mix crab, bacon, and cornstarch.  Set aside.

Place crabmeat mixture on crust.  Sprinkle with Swiss cheese.   Pour half-and-half mixture over all.  Drizzle with Topping ingredients.

Can line a 9"x 13" dish with pastry.  Fill as above.  Bake at 375° for 20 – 30 minutes.  Cut into 15 appetizers.

Place the butter in a 9" square or 7" x 11" baking dish.  Microwave on high for 40 seconds, or until butter is melted.  Stir in the sugar and spread over bottom of dish.  Cover with the cherries and plums, and then sprinkle the orange rind over.  Arrange the challah over the fruit in one layer.  Set aside.

Bake at 350° for 35 minutes until puffed, golden-brown, and center is firm to touch.  Serve at once.  Spoon juices over toast.
Cut squash in half and remove seeds and membranes.

Cut fish into 4 - 6  equal pieces.
Place salmon skin-side down in a shallow dish that has been sprayed with vegetable cooking spray.
Combine remaining ingredients.  Pour over fish.
In a small bowl, mix ½ cup reserved apricot liquid (add extra nectar if not enough) with melted margarine, orange juice and rind.  Pour mixture over layers.

Scrub potatoes.  Place on baking sheet and bake at 400° for 40 minutes or until tender when pierced with a fork.  (Or you can microwave them until tender.)  Cool; peel and cut into lengthwise slices about ¼-inch thick.
Microwave on high, flesh side down, in ¼ cup water for approximately 8-10 minutes, or until tender.
Melt ½ cup margarine in a large skillet.  Add celery and onion and sauté for 10 minutes.  Transfer to a large bowl.

Heat remaining ½ cup margarine and stock in small saucepan until margarine melts.  Pour over stuffing mixture and add remaining ½ cup Grand Marnier.  Stir well to moisten stuffing.  Season with thyme and pepper.
Cook 1 lb. pitted prunes with lemon, sugar, and ½ c. water.  Chop prunes to desired consistency.  Add ½ c. finely ground nuts (she uses walnuts), juice of ½ lemon (1 tbsp.), and rind of orange.

Combine spinach, onions, pepper, and margarine; spread in 10" casserole.  Sauté mushrooms in nonstick skillet sprayed w/ cooking spray until mushrooms are brown; drain.  Sprinkle ½ cup cheddar cheese over spinach.  Arrange mushrooms on top and season with garlic powder.   Cover with remaining cheese.  Can cover and refrigerate until ready to bake. Place 1 cup of flour, confectioners’ sugar, and butter in food processor.  Pulse until the mixture resembles coarse meal.  Add the sour cream and vanilla extract.  Process briefly until the dough is just moistened.  Press the dough evenly into the bottom and ½ inch up the sides of a 9-inch square baking pan.  Bake the crust until it is pale golden, about 20 minutes.
Place fruit in a greased 9" x 13" x 2" baking dish.  Cover with the ½ cup sugar and the 2 tbsp. flour and pour on the water.

Cook pears, cherries, brown sugar, and rosemary in a 4- to 5-quart heavy pot over moderate heat, stirring, until pears are tender, about 20 minutes. This recipe can be prepared on the stove or in an electric pressure cooker. The ingredients and most of the steps are identical for both cooking methods. This style of risotto goes best with seafood, such as shrimp, pan-seared scallops or crab cakes.
If cooking on the stove, heat up 4 cups of chicken stock/broth in a separate pot, and keep heated throughout the cooking process.

Heat olive oil and 2 tbsp butter in a second pot on the stove or on SAUTE setting of the electric pressure cooker. Place the other 2 tbsp of butter back in the fridge to keep it cold. Add the diced shallots and sauté 2-3 minutes. Add the arborio rice and toast for an additional 2-3 minutes.

Add the white wine and gently stir for a few minutes. If making in the pressure cooker, be sure to cook off all the alcohol before moving to the next step (you can tell by smelling it if the alcohol is still present).

_Stovetop:_ Working a ladle (~¼ cup) at a time, add hot broth to the rice and gently stir until well absorbed. Rice does not require constant stirring but should be stirred every 30 seconds.  The broth will initially absorb quickly but towards the end each ladle may take 2-3 minutes. After all broth has been absorbed, remove from heat and let stand, 2-3 minutes.

_Pressure cooker:_ Heat 2 cups of broth in the microwave on high for 1 minute. While this is not required, it should help it come to pressure faster. Once all the alcohol has been cooked off, hit Start/Stop to turn off sauté mode, pour in the broth and give everything a nice stir to make sure nothing sticks to the bottom of the pot. Carefully close and lock the lid and close the pressure seal. Set the pressure cooker to HIGH for 6 minutes. (Reminder: it will take several minutes to come to pressure before the 6 minute timer engages.) When the timer goes off, immediately quick release the pressure. Once all the steam has been released and the lid is unlocked, remove the lid. If, after opening the lid, it appears too liquidy, you may turn it back to saute for a few minutes, stirring gently until it reaches the proper consistency. Turn off and let stand 2-3 minutes.
After thickening for a few minutes, stir in the grated cheese and additional 2 tbsp of cold butter. Serve immediately.

_Optional stir-ins:_ Add some texture and umami by stirring in some sauteed mushrooms and pancetta. After adding the second-to-last ladle of broth on the stove or once the pressure cooker comes to pressure, heat oil in a skillet. Add diced mushrooms and sauté over medium high heat for 4-5 minutes. Add diced pancetta and cook for one more minute, then remove from heat. Stir into the risotto after adding the cheese and butter. For a sweeter iteration, stir in roasted butternut squash cubes and candied pecans or walnuts.

Remove the skin and any added seasonings from the guanciale. Cut into cubes. Ensure each piece has both meat and fat. Sauté over medium-high heat until fat is released and outside is crispy. Remove from heat. Reserve the fat and set the guanciale aside.

Cook pasta according to directions. Meanwhile, separate the eggs. Discard the whites (or save for another use) and place the yolks in a metal bowl (the bowl for a double-boiler is perfect). Add parmesan, pecorino and black pepper and whisk vigorously to form a paste. Add 2 tablespoons of guanciale fat and some hot pasta water (start with a half ladle or ⅛ cup).

To pasteurize the eggs, whisk vigorously over boiling water. As you stir over the heat, you should see the sauce become creamier. Be very careful not to get too close to the heat and never rest the sauce bowl on top of the pasta pot like a double boiler - you do not want to cook the eggs!

When the pasta is cooked al dente, add the guanciale and the pasta directly to the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce texture isn't quite right, add more grated cheese or pasta water. Plate and top with grated parmesan.

Remove the outer skin/seasoning from the guanciale, and cut into chunks. Make sure each chunk has a mix of meat and fat. Sauté over medium heat until the fat has rendered and the meat is chewy/crispy.

Once the guanciale is done, deglaze the pan with white wine, stirring to combine with the rendered guanciale fat. With a slotted spoon, remove most of the guanciale and set aside, leaving behind all the wine/fat and some guanciale for added flavor (ideally any pieces that didn't cook as quickly).
Melt butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat.  Sauté onions, mushrooms, and shrimp, if using, until soft.  Cut shrimp into bite-sized pieces.

In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs (can use electric mixer).  Add all other ingredients except ½ cup of the cheese.  Pour into a greased ovenproof 2-quart casserole.  (I use 7" x 11" Pyrex baking dish.)

Bake uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes or until mixture is set.  Remove from oven and sprinkle with remaining cheese.  (Use extra cheese, if needed, to lightly cover entire top.)  Continue to bake until cheese melts.
